Answer: A
Reason: Figure 1a shows a significant right pleural effusion occupying the lower thoracic cavity, while Figure 1b reveals extensive mediastinal gas and fluid consistent with an abscess. In the context of an aorto-esophageal fistula or esophageal perforation, the right-sided effusion is typically larger due to anatomical drainage patterns and is directly caused by the leakage of contents from the mediastinal infection into the pleural space.
